comparison: Perfect alignment on beta oscillation findings (C55-C57, C59, C143). Both evaluations support age-dependent modulation of beta oscillations with consistent spatial localization. OpenEval provides specific statistical details (R²=0.29, p=4×10⁻⁵) while peer reviewers affirm findings are 'well localized' and 'compelling.'

Perfect alignment on burst model findings (C68-C69, C112-C113, C144-C145). Both evaluations support that burst probability explains task-induced beta modulation and shows age-related changes. OpenEval emphasizes strong correlation (R²=0.50) and consistency with Rayson et al. 2023, while peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'pan-spectral burst probability' modulation with age.

Strong alignment on connectivity findings (C63-C64, C67, C143). Both evaluations support age-related connectivity changes with spatial specificity. OpenEval provides quantitative details (R²=0.42, p=2.67×10⁻⁷) and cites supporting literature, while peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'connectivity' as one of the key age-modulated findings.

Strong alignment on burst spectral properties (C74-C77, C114, C146). Both evaluations support age-related changes in spectral content. OpenEval notes that amplitude remains stable while frequency content changes, while peer reviewers confirm 'pan-spectral burst probability' findings as part of well-supported conclusions.

Strong alignment on OPM-MEG system validation (C47-C54, C82-C85, C90). Both evaluations support successful deployment across wide age range. OpenEval emphasizes technical specifications, high retention rates (27/27 children), and helmet design validation, while peer reviewers affirm the system 'allows free head movement scanning with relatively high ratio of usable trials.'

Strong alignment on OPM-MEG significance for developmental research (C91, C147). Both evaluations support that OPM-MEG is validated and ideal for neurodevelopmental studies. OpenEval emphasizes extension to 2-year-olds as substantial advance, while peer reviewers state it is 'quite practical and easy to deploy' with 'performance as good as conventional MEG.'

Both address methodological controls for head size confounds (C79-C81). OpenEval explicitly evaluates statistical analysis and simulations confirming helmet design controlled for head size, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these controls by stating conclusions are 'mostly well supported by data acquired under proper method.'

Both address lack of finger-specific somatotopy (C58). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to multiple methodological limitations (C122-C128) that could explain null result, while peer reviewers appear to accept the finding without challenge, noting beta oscillations are 'well localized' overall.

Both address burst amplitude stability with age (C73). OpenEval supports this null finding as part of broader pattern showing frequency redistribution rather than signal strength changes, while peer reviewers implicitly accept it as part of 'mostly well supported' conclusions.

Minimal overlap on interpretive context. OpenEval R7 discusses mechanistic interpretation and agreement with prior literature (C115-C117), while peer R3 focuses on connectivity findings. Both reference Schäfer et al. 2014 (C117) but in different contexts.

OpenEval evaluates methodological limitations regarding trial design (C129-C135), acknowledging that short trials prevent separation of PMBR from baseline. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not explicitly address these design trade-offs.

OpenEval evaluates control analysis for differential trial loss (C136-C138), finding results unchanged when trial counts equalized. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not explicitly address this potential confound.

OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN the impact of limited temporal sensor coverage on connectivity findings (C139-C142), noting speculation about whether patterns reflect biology or methodology. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval evaluates discussion of system limitations and future directions (C100-C108), including helmet weight concerns and suggestions for improvements. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific limitations.

OpenEval evaluates background literature on beta oscillations (C1-C24) as appropriately cited and supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not explicitly evaluate background claims.
